items.title: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on Washington’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.text: A rough Cardinals defense could get Burks into the deep league conversation, but he’s had just six targets in two games since returning from the bye week. If he doesn’t do something this week, Brandon Aiyuk might be knocking on the door of his starting spot come Week 13. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on the Jaguars’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
items.text: Meyers will expectedly function as the Jaguars’ No. 1 wide receiver with Parker Washington (shoulder) sidelined and considered week-to-week. Meyers accordingly vaults into the WR2/3 range and could deliver a big stat line against a soft Titans defense. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Rashod Bateman (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.text: You know what you’re getting into if you start Bateman, but he did manage a touchdown grab against the Panthers last week and the Ravens have generally pumped up their passing usage since Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore. He’s probably a bit below the FLEX line in standard leagues, but it wouldn’t shock us if he landed in that area this week against the Texans. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Jaguars ruled out Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) for Week 12 against the Titans.
items.text: Chris Rodriguez should be added wherever he is available. Tuten will finally take a week off after playing through foot and ankle injuries for multiple weeks. He reportedly aggravated the issues in Week 11 against the Giants. Hopefully, Tuten will return for the Jaguars’ expectedly fantasy-friendly game against the Bears in Week 13. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Zay Flowers (ankle) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.text: He can be started as a low-end WR1 against a Texans outfit that has given up plenty of passing yards this year. Flowers has been a fixture on the injury report this year but hasn’t missed a game since Week 2. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Derrick Henry (concussion) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.text: He’ll get his normal workload, though he’s playing like more of a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 since the Jacoby Brissett takeover, against the Texans. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
items.text: Hunter didn’t practice at any point this week. The hamstring injury has been described as short-term, but this is the third straight week he’ll miss with it. Perhaps he’ll have a chance to get back for Week 13. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Kayshon Boutte (hip) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
items.text: Boutte did not practice at any point this week and has essentially become a boom-bust FLEX threat at best on a limited snap count. He is likely questionable for Week 13 and can be dropped in shallow leagues. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.text: With Kayshon Boutte out, it’s possible that Harrison could be Houston’s No. 3 wideout if they continue to manage things delicately with Tank Dell. He’ll be a tough FLEX play given his snap volume with the Texans even despite a nice matchup against the Ravens. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Browns.
items.text: We can’t know for sure, but it looks like the Raiders might choose to hold Bowers out through their Week 13 bye. He was limited on Wednesday, and although he was limited again on Thursday, he practiced with his injured ankle heavily taped. Today, he sat out. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak tends to let his players take the field on game day, even if they are at less than 100 percent, but Bowers must be viewed as truly questionable at best. If active, he should be in fantasy football lineups. In the meantime, make a backup plan. - Nic Bodiford
